notable_absence.finding:
Per the round context's explicit instruction to decide, per page, whether reusing sdk:subdocument-operations is warranted: this record does NOT link eventing:lookupin-subdocument-operation to sdk:subdocument-operations, because this page gives no textual basis for asserting any relationship between them (it never mentions the SDK or its lookupIn API at all) - the evidence gate requires a real page quote to support any relation, and none exists here. They are analogous surfaces (both are path-level reads against a specific field inside a document) reached through completely different APIs (couchbase.lookupIn/couchbase.LookupInSpec.get inside a JS handler vs an SDK client method), and this record treats them as a described-but-unlinked analogy rather than forcing a graph edge.

Separately: this page's OnUpdate signature is `function OnUpdate(doc, meta, xattrs) {` - a third parameter, `xattrs`, that does not appear in any other OnUpdate signature in this batch (all others are `OnUpdate(doc, meta)`) and is never referenced in the function body (only `meta.id` is used). The registry's eventing:on-update-handler concept (recurrence 18) has no documented third parameter. This looks like a copy-paste artifact from the nearby `{"xattrs": false}` option literal on `LookupInSpec.get(...)`, not a real, documented handler-signature extension - worth a docs-issue rather than a concept, since minting a concept from an apparent typo would misrepresent the API.
